COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
C528 No.1266 of 2025
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
Mr. Amanjot Singh Chadha, learned counsel for the 
Applicant.
2. Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned AGA, for the State/1.
3. The present criminal miscellaneous application filed 
under C528 of BNSS, is with a prayer that the proceedings in 
criminal miscellaneous case no.174/2024, under section 12 of 
the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, 
“Shrimati Monika Pal Vs. Ashutosh Kumar and others”, 
pending before the court of learned ACJM, Kashipur, District 
Udham Singh Nagar, be quashed.
4. The applicant has also made a prayer for interim relief 
vide paper no.46.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Applicant 
makes a statement with reference to paper no.44 and 45, 
which is an order of this Court, passed in C528 No.1012 of 
2025, that in a similar matter, wherein Respondent No.2 was 
the complainant and wherein the Court was pleased to grant 
an interim relief. Learned counsel makes a submission that in 
the said case as paper no.44 and 45, the next date fixed is 26th
August, 2025.
6. Admit.
7. Issue notice to the Respondent No.2. Steps to be taken 
within a week. Counter affidavit to be filed within a period of 
three weeks.
8. Till the next date of listing, the entire proceedings of
criminal miscellaneous case no.174/2024, under section 12 of 
the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005,  “Shrimati Monika Pal Vs. Ashutosh Kumar and others”, 
pending before the court of learned ACJM, Kashipur, District 
Udham Singh Nagar, shall remain stayed.
9. List this matter along with C528 No.1012 of 2025.
10. Stay application (IA No.1/2025) stands disposed of 
accordingly. 
 (Ashish Naithani, J.) 
 11.08.2025
Nitesh/

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
C-528 No.1266 of 2025
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Amanjot Singh Chadha, 
learned counsel for the applicants.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Addl. 
Advocate General along with Mr. S.C. 
Dumka, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Prince Chauhan, learned 
counsel for respondent no.2.
4. In the morning session, the matter 
was referred to mediation.
5. The mediation report has been 
received. It records that the parties 
have amicably settled their disputes on 
agreed terms and conditions, and that 
the mediation proceedings were 
successful.
6. Learned counsel for respondent 
no. 2 (wife) submits that applicant no. 
1 (husband) shall pay a total sum of 
₹14,50,000/- to respondent no. 2 
towards permanent alimony in full and
final settlement of all claims; that, the 
parties shall initiate proceedings under 
Section 27 of the U.C.C; that, at the 
time of the first motion in the said 
proceedings, applicant no. 1 shall pay 
₹7,25,000/- to respondent no. 2 and 
shall also return the gold ornaments as 
enumerated in the inventory annexed 
to and identified in the settlement 
agreement. The balance amount of 
₹7,25,000 (Rupees seven lakh twenty- five thousand only) shall be paid by 
applicant no. 1 at the time of the 
second motion in the proceedings 
under Section 27 of the U.C.C.
7. Learned counsel for the parties 
prays for and is granted three weeks’ 
time to file appropriate application.
8. List on 30.06.2026.
9. Interim order dated 11.08.2025 to 
continue till the next date of listing.
(Alok Mahra, J.) 18.05.2026 Mamta
